cards.text: Welcome to Sparkle's station, friend! We're in a collection of Solomon's proverbs that the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, copied down (Proverbs 25:1). This chapter opens with snow in summer and rain at harvest, two things that just don't belong.

cards.question: Solomon says something suits a fool about as well as snow in summer. What is it?

cards.text: Next comes a fluttering sparrow and a darting swallow. It's like a fly in my bakery while I'm frosting: circling, circling, circling, and NEVER landing.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says every curse spoken against you is sure to land on you.

cards.text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools. I read that list real slow the first time, just making sure cookie stampers weren't on it.

cards.question: Solomon says do not answer a fool according to his folly. Why not?

answers.text: Or you'll end up like him

cards.text: Then the VERY next line starts with "Answer a fool according to his folly" and friend, my first week here I read those two lines back and forth until my eyebrows got tired.

cards.question: Solomon gives a reason to answer a fool according to his folly, too. What is it?

answers.text: So he won't be wise in his own eyes
So he'll finally stop talking to you
So other people won't follow him

cards.text: Now here's a job Solomon says you should NOT hand to a fool. He says doing it is like cutting off your own feet, or drinking violence.

cards.question: Sending a ___ by the hand of a fool is like cutting off your own feet.

cards.text: That's like trusting the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, and they SWORE they still had a charge. Next picture: lame legs hanging limp.

cards.question: Solomon says a ___ in the mouth of a fool is like lame legs hanging limp.
Solomon pictures a stone tied right into a sling. True or false: he says that's like giving honor to a fool.

cards.text: Solomon comes back to the proverb: in a fool's mouth, it's like a thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkard. Then he pictures an archer who wounds at random.

cards.question: Who does Solomon say is like an archer who wounds at random?

answers.text: The one who hires a fool or passerby
The one who trusts a fool's advice
The one who walks along with fools

cards.text: Then comes the line everybody remembers, whether they want to or not: a dog going back to its own vomit.

cards.question: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool ___ his folly.

cards.text: That's me and the snooze button, every morning, five times, like I've never met it before. Then Solomon points at somebody in even worse shape than a fool.

cards.question: Who does Solomon say has less hope than a fool?

answers.text: A man wise in his own eyes
A man who loves to argue

cards.question: True or false: Solomon already used the words "wise in his own eyes" earlier in this chapter.

cards.text: Now a new character shuffles in: the slacker. And friend, he has a BIG announcement.

cards.question: What does the slacker announce?

answers.text: A lion is in the road

cards.text: A fierce lion in the PUBLIC SQUARE? I've heard "my car won't start," I've heard "my alarm didn't go off," but I have NEVER heard "there's a lion at the bus stop."

cards.question: Solomon compares the slacker to a door. As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his ___.

cards.text: Then it's mealtime. The slacker buries his hand in the dish.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the slacker eats so fast that he empties the dish.

cards.text: His hand is IN the dish, and it wears him out just to bring it back to his mouth. I spent years not moving in the back of a drawer, and even I'm impressed.

cards.question: The slacker can barely lift his hand. But how wise does he think he is?

answers.text: Wiser than seven men who answer discreetly
Wiser than all of the king's advisers
Wiser than the elders at the city gate

cards.text: Next, Solomon turns to a passerby who meddles in a quarrel that isn't his own.

cards.question: Solomon says a passerby who meddles in someone else's quarrel is like one who grabs a ___ by the ears.

cards.text: Picture it: the dog AND both people in the argument all turn around and look at YOU. Then Solomon pictures a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says that madman is like a man who deceives his neighbor and then says he was only joking.

cards.text: Friend, saying you were only joking doesn't put the arrows back. Now Solomon talks about what keeps a fire going.

cards.question: Without ___, a fire goes out; without ___, a conflict ceases.

cards.text: Charcoal for embers, wood for fire, and a quarrelsome man for kindling strife. Every workplace has one: you mention the weather, and somehow there's a fight.

cards.question: Solomon says the words of a gossip are like choice morsels. Where do they go?

answers.text: Out of the mouth and away

cards.text: Choice morsels? Friend, I bake for a living, and NOBODY stops at one cookie. Next picture: a clay pot covered in glaze.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says glaze covering a clay pot is like a wise man's kind words.

cards.text: Solomon says that glaze is like burning lips and a wicked heart, which is basically pretty icing on a cookie that's raw in the middle. Then he spells it out: a hateful man disguises himself with his speech, but he lays up deceit in his heart.

cards.question: When that hateful man speaks graciously, what does Solomon say to do?
True or false: Solomon says the hateful man's hidden wickedness will stay hidden for good.

cards.text: Now picture a man digging a pit.

cards.question: What does Solomon say happens to the one who digs a pit?

answers.text: He's made to fill it in

cards.text: And whoever rolls a stone will have it roll back on him. I once rolled a rolling pin across the counter to show off, and it came RIGHT back and smacked my gold base.

cards.question: The chapter ends with a lying tongue that hates those it crushes. And a flattering mouth causes ___.

findings.problem: Solomon appears here for the first time, but the card never says who he is. Hezekiah gets an introduction (king of Judah) and Solomon does not.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Proverbs 26:2 is about an undeserved curse. No card ever says "undeserved." Card 3 tells only the birds, and card 4 asks about "every curse." The baker can leave thinking no curse ever lands, which misses the verse's key qualifier.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 11 gives only the picture "lame legs hanging limp," so nothing points to "proverb" over "promise" or "secret." A promise or a secret in a fool's mouth fits the picture just as well, so the pick comes down to luck. It also tests wording the baker hasn't seen.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 2 follow a fixed repeating pattern: multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, then multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false again (cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
